finding.description: Profiles q-42531, q-130451 and q-91162 always retain the correct first coefficient in their extra unit-coefficient distractor. Consequently, that signed coefficient appears three times while its negation appears twice. Learners can recover the first operation without inspecting the matrices and calculate only the second. This order-independent shortcut affects two surviving records in the exact five-record batch.
finding.reproduction: Run the context Python with `-B reproduce_shortcut.py` from evidence_root; expected exit 1. Minimal case: profile=q-42531, seed=472, A=[[1,2,3],[2,5,4],[-3,7,8]], pivot=0, column=0, ks=[0,-2,3]. Bank pairs are [(-2,-1),(2,-3),(-2,3),(-2,-3),(2,3)]. Frequency reveals -2; calculating only the second coefficient selects the accepted pair (-2,3). See counterfactual-records.json and shortcut-grader-report.json.
finding.requested_change: Revise generalized unit-perturbation recipes so the extra distractor does not invariably preserve the correct first coefficient. Vary eligible coefficient roles and signs while preserving distinct choices, source replay and the two-operation skill. Retain the reproduction as a regression, verify the predictor fails across recognizable bank subgroups after delivery, and regenerate the candidate batch. Do not remove source families or modify original inventory questions.

finding.description: Batch-selection failure: identify the unique magnitude-pattern outlier, take the dominant first magnitude with the opposite outlier first sign, and calculate only the second operation. This bypass succeeds on all five delivered records, including both recognizable bank subgroups: unit-first 2/2 and swapped-magnitude 3/3. Broader generator controls contain counterexamples.
finding.reproduction: From evidence_root run `/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/.venv/bin/python -B reproduce_batch_shortcut.py`; expected exit 1. Minimal instance: q-42531, seed 1278010737, A=[[-1,4,7],[8,-5,-9],[10,-1,-9]], pivot=2, column=1. Bank pairs are [(-1,5),(-4,-5),(4,5),(4,-5),(-4,5)]. Outlier (-1,5) predicts first coefficient +4; calculating only the second coefficient gives accepted pair (4,-5). Complete batch and native-grader evidence are retained.
finding.requested_change: Regenerate the candidate batch and add a batch acceptance check preventing this uniform outlier-sign relationship across the delivered pool. Retain the runnable regression and verify cue-breaking examples survive delivery. Preserve the repaired independent-sign construction and source families; no database or original-source edits are required.
